prompt: Apply the Null Object pattern: complete the do-nothing SilentLog and make AuditedCart substitute it for a null log in the constructor, so add() never needs a null check.
explanation: A null object is a real implementation of the interface whose methods do nothing harmless. Substituting it once, in the constructor, means every other method can call log.record(...) unconditionally -- the null check exists in exactly one place instead of being repeated everywhere. Because log is final and never null after construction, log() can also promise a non-null result.
hints: The constructor needs a single conditional: use the incoming log when it is not null, otherwise create a SilentLog.
SilentLog.record is meant to have an empty body -- that is the whole point of the pattern.
add() should update total and then call log.record("add " + item + " x" + quantity) without testing log.
